subject: Tiered subprocessors, conditional-access controls, and TIA scope
messages:
From: Mia Roberts <mia.roberts@medicorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Data Procurement <data-procurement@medicorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Question on subprocessors & conditional access for EU patient data

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Before procurement moves this forward we need a clear mapping of how Redwood handles international transfers, especially for EU patient data. A few specific asks from legal and our security team:  

- Can you confirm which downstream subprocessors handle PHI-enriched payloads and whether you operate tiered subprocessors (i.e., partner->subcontractor chains)? We need a short inventory and segregation by region.
- We have a strict conditional-access requirement: only services that support customer-enforced IP whitelisting / conditional VPC peering and per-customer KMS key separation can process EU data in production. Does Redwood offer config options to enforce that?
- For transfers involving the UK, do you rely on SCCs alone or also the UK IDTA/UK Addendum? Our UK privacy counsel expects explicit evidence of the addendum or equivalent controls.
- Finally, we need a TIA/DTIA mapping showing where data flows, whether logs or telemetry leave the EU, and a proposed mitigation plan.

Target deadline from procurement: 2028-04-18 EOD (our CFO is gating the budget). Can you confirm whether you can deliver a draft TIA + subprocessor inventory by then?

Appreciate the quick help — looped in procurement above for timeline visibility.

Best,
Mia Roberts
Head of Data Procurement
MediCorp Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mia Roberts <mia.roberts@medicorp.com>
Cc: Data Procurement <data-procurement@medicorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T12:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question on subprocessors & conditional access for EU patient data

Hi Mia — thanks for the clear list. We can get that to you by your deadline. High-level answers up front, with an attached starter pack: redwood-tia-mapping.pdf (TIA mapping) and subprocessor_inventory_q2_2028.csv (current inventory).

- Tiered subprocessors: yes, we use a small set of tier-1 subprocessors (cloud infra, telemetry, observability) and some tier-2 partners (managed services for specialized accelerators). The CSV flags which subprocessors may be involved in PHI pipelines and which are region-restricted to EU-only.
- Conditional access and KMS: Redwood Private and Dedicated options support customer-managed VPC peering and KMS key separation. For hosted plans we offer strong isolation and customer-level encryption keys for model payloads, but we generally recommend Dedicated for strict KMS separation.
- UK transfers: we maintain SCCs and a UK Addendum template; I will ask Legal to provide the current draft and evidence.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura (Legal) to confirm UK wording and whether the addendum suffices for MediCorp's counsel.
2) Vivek (Infra) to provide the region routing and conditional-access technical specifics.
3) We’ll deliver the TIA stub + subprocessor list by 2028-04-18 and update it with your feedback.

Attaching the two files now and will loop in Laura and Vivek. If procurement needs a tighter SLA exception for EU-only routing let me know and we can scope it in the proposal.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-tia-mapping.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_q2_2028.csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mia Roberts <mia.roberts@medicorp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Data Procurement <data-procurement@medicorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question on subprocessors & conditional access for EU patient data

Hi Mia / Jonas — looping in on the legal side.

A few clarifications from our counsel:  

- UK: For processing connected to UK-residency data we provide the EU SCCs (post‑Schrems II adjustments) and a UK Addendum (equivalent to the IDTA/UK Addendum). The addendum is our standard template; where customers require, we can accept redlines on a limited set of clauses (data localization, audit rights, subprocessor approval).
- TIA scope: the TIA we attached is a high-level mapping; we will produce a DTIA variant showing telemetry/logging retention and if/where system diagnostics may traverse non-EU routes. For PHI use cases we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments to avoid any telemetry leaving the customer region.
- Subprocessors: the CSV Jonas attached includes a column "processing_scope" and flags for PHI. We can also produce a short narrative describing controls at each tier (access controls, encryption at-rest, SOC 2 considerations).

I’ve attached the current UK Addendum draft for your counsel to review (redwood-uk-addendum-draft.docx). If MediCorp requires KMS separation enforced by contract, we will need to add a contract amendment referencing key custody and rotation responsibilities — this is routine but will need procurement sign-off.

Happy to hop on a quick call if your counsel wants to walk the draft. If you prefer we can do an initial markup and return a negotiated addendum by 2028-04-17 to meet your budget cadence.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-uk-addendum-draft.docx)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Mia Roberts <mia.roberts@medicorp.com>
Cc: Data Procurement <data-procurement@medicorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T14:07:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question on subprocessors & conditional access for EU patient data

Mia — quick technical note from infra:  

- Region routing: For EU-only commitments we can pin workloads to eu-west-1 (and mirror backup to eu-central-1 on request). We instrument routing policies so inference traffic and KV caches stay in-region; audit logs can be configured to store in-customer S3 (or equivalent) under your control.
- Conditional-access options: Dedicated + Private support VPC peering, customer IP allowlists, and forced egress via customer-managed NAT. For hosted customers we offer token-level scoping and IP allowlist. Per-customer KMS separation is available on Dedicated and Private.
- Observability/telemetry: Service-level telemetry (errors/latency) is aggregated and may be stored in our observability backend (US/EU regions). For PHI customers we can route observability to your VPC and truncate payloads.

Operational ask: if MediCorp requires contractual assurance that telemetry will not leave the EU, we can include a routing guarantee clause and an SLA for routing exceptions; that would be a limited SLA exception we need Procurement to agree on.

If helpful I can add a short appendix to the TIA that lists the exact kernel/agent pieces that could generate logs and where they live.

—Vivek
VP Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

From: Mia Roberts <mia.roberts@medicorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Data Procurement <data-procurement@medicorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T16:21:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question on subprocessors & conditional access for EU patient data

Thanks everyone — that is very helpful.

Next steps we need from Redwood by 2028-04-18 EOD:  
1) Updated TIA/DTIA mapping that explicitly calls out any telemetry paths and confirms region pinning (PDF fine).
2) Subprocessor inventory annotated for PHI (CSV okay).
3) UK Addendum draft (Word) with notes where legal redlines are likely required.
4) DocuSign-ready contract or link for a routing guarantee / KMS separation amendment if possible.

If you can provide those artifacts I will route to our counsel and procurement and we’ll aim to close the purchase order. Please provide the DocuSign link (or a HubSpot attachment) when available.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to schedule a 30-minute call if any of you want to talk through the DTIA appendix.

Best,
Mia
MediCorp Health
